_note: Snapshot of portotechhub.com/conference-2026/schedule (Sessionize) for Porto Tech Hub 2026 (10 November 2026, Alfândega do Porto). Welcome and goodbye blocks are excluded. Co-speakers reduced to primary speaker to fit the one-speaker-per-session model. Abstracts trimmed.

speakers.name: Willem Jan Glerum
speakers.bio: Principal Software Engineer at Lunatech. Focused on Quarkus, cloud, and security.

sessions.title: Practical MCP Security in Action
sessions.speaker: Willem Jan Glerum
sessions.abstract: MCP authorization is OAuth 2.1 done right. Quarkus makes it tractable. Governance matters more than the token format.

sessions.title: Implementing AI Architecture Patterns with Enterprise Java
sessions.speaker: Otavio Santana
sessions.abstract: Artificial Intelligence is quickly transitioning from experimentation to enterprise software.

sessions.title: AI-Native Observability: Building Self-Debugging Next.js Applications with OpenTelemetry
sessions.speaker: Andrei Tazetdinov
sessions.abstract: Modern applications generate more telemetry than engineers can realistically consume. Dashboards multiply, alerts become noisy, and finding the root cause of a production issue often requires navigating dozens of tools, traces, and logs.

sessions.title: Fundamentals of Software Engineering in the age of AI
sessions.speaker: Dan Vega
sessions.abstract: Every few years, something comes along that's supposed to end software engineering as we know it. IDE features that write code for you. Low-code. No-code. Now AI. And every time, the role adapts, the fundamentals stay, and the people who understand the craft come out ahead.

sessions.title: The Agentic Loops Every Developer Should Know
sessions.speaker: Rui Quintino
sessions.abstract: Loops are a key primitive for autonomous AI agents, and the now widely used "Agent Mode". This session dives into the journey from the core Reason + Act loop to loop engineering — the shift from prompting agents to designing the systems that prompt them.

sessions.title: Comparing Promises, Observables, and Signals
sessions.speaker: Lance Finney
sessions.abstract: Since JavaScript is single threaded, special techniques are necessary for asynchronous and reactive programming. Promises were introduced a few years ago to enable asynchronous programming without the dreaded "callback hell".

sessions.title: WordPress in 2027: Reinventing a Giant in the Age of AI
sessions.speaker: Carlos Moreira
sessions.abstract: Artificial Intelligence is changing the way we create, manage, and consume content on the web. AI agents, automation, and new tools are transforming the role of websites and content management platforms. In this session, we'll explore how WordPress is evolving to meet this new reality.

sessions.title: Building Fast AI Search and Automation with GraalVM
sessions.speaker: Alina Yurenko
sessions.abstract: AI features might be easy to prototype, but as you add more features and dependencies, they can become bulky, slow to start, and hard to deploy.

sessions.title: Back to the Future: AI Workflows, Cross-Compiling, and the Magic of Amiga Custom Chips
sessions.speaker: Torsten Hopf
sessions.abstract: Developing for retro hardware is notorious for its steep learning curve: missing stack traces, cryptic hardware registers, and assembly manuals that read like ancient texts. But what if we could bypass this pain using today’s most advanced paradigms?

sessions.title: FinOps: Beyond Cost Reduction
sessions.speaker: Eduardo Piairo
sessions.abstract: FinOps is an operational framework and a cultural practice that maximizes the business value of cloud... you can find the definition on the FinOps Foundation site ( https://www.finops.org/introduction/what-is-finops/ ).

sessions.title: Comparing Agentic AI Frameworks for Java
sessions.speaker: Sandra Ahlgrimm
sessions.abstract: Agentic AI marks a shift from passive, prompt-driven interactions to autonomous systems that can reason, plan, and execute work. On the JVM, several frameworks are emerging to support this new paradigm, but they take very different approaches.

sessions.title: Mastering Kubernetes Scheduling
sessions.speaker: Ricardo Castro
sessions.abstract: Pod placement decisions can make or break your cluster's reliability, cost efficiency, and performance — yet most engineers only scratch the surface of what Kubernetes scheduling offers. This talk is structured as a progressive deep dive.

sessions.title: Tokenmaxxing: What Observability Can Teach Us About AI
sessions.speaker: Hélia Barroso
sessions.abstract: It's hard to escape the constant headlines about AI and the latest metric everyone seems to be celebrating: tokens.

sessions.title: How to survive and thrive as a dev (team) in the exponential age of real-world AI
sessions.speaker: Sander Hoogendoorn
sessions.abstract: The AI revolution isn’t coming — it’s already altering how we architect products, ship features, and run engineering teams.

sessions.title: Your Biggest New Customer Can't See Pixels
sessions.speaker: Tim Damen
sessions.abstract: For decades we've argued that accessibility is the right thing to do. The argument just got a lot easier, because your next customer probably isn't human. Whether you like it or not AI agents from are now browsing, comparing, and interacting on behalf of users.

sessions.title: Scotty I need Warp Speed - Ways to improve JVM startup
sessions.speaker: Gerrit Grunwald
sessions.abstract: When running Java in the cloud, the JVM startup time can become a limitation. Especially when you look at spinning up new instances of an app as response to changes in load, the warmup time can be a problem.

sessions.title: Drogonsec: SAST + SCA + Secrets + IaC in one open-source scanner
sessions.speaker: Filipi Pires
sessions.abstract: Drogonsec is an open-source, high-performance security scanner built for developers and CI/CD pipelines.

sessions.title: From Prompts to Workflows: Building Agentic AI with LangChain4j
sessions.speaker: Alex Soto
sessions.abstract: Large Language Models are no longer just answering questions. They are becoming agents that plan, call tools, loop until quality is high, and even ask humans for help.

sessions.title: Building Reliable Agentic Systems: Lessons from Operating AI Infrastructure at Scale
sessions.speaker: Nishant Gupta
sessions.abstract: AI agents are rapidly evolving from chat interfaces into autonomous systems capable of reasoning, planning, using tools, and taking actions across complex environments.

sessions.title: Fan #0’s Journey: What Nobody Tells You About Building a Community
sessions.speaker: Pedro Fonseca
sessions.abstract: Building a tech community sounds amazing on paper, but the reality for "Fan #0" is packed with friction and frustration. In this 25-minute session, we strip away the romance of community entrepreneurship to share the real story behind the birth of Raycafé Porto.

sessions.title: Building Multi-Agent Systems with Spring AI & Redis
sessions.speaker: Raphael De Lio
sessions.abstract: AI systems are moving beyond single-model architectures. The future is multi-agent where multiple specialized agents collaborate, share context, and make decisions together.

sessions.title: From Zero to Agentic Query in One Afternoon: Build a GraphQL API and Expose It to an LLM Agent
sessions.speaker: Željko Kozina
sessions.abstract: In this hands-on workshop, you'll go from an empty project to a working GraphQL API that an LLM agent can discover and query on its own. No prior GraphQL experience required; basic Spring Boot knowledge is a hard requirement!

sessions.title: Coding assistants: a journey from a convert
sessions.speaker: Nicolas Fränkel
sessions.abstract: For a long time, I was advert to coding assistants. I didn't see any benefit: it was faster for me to write code, than to let them generate crap, and fix it afterwards. Then, around summer 2025, something changed. At home, I used Claude Code for better and better results.

sessions.title: Building AI Agents That Don’t Betray You: Practical Security Patterns for Business Workflows
sessions.speaker: Agnieszka Chojka
sessions.abstract: AI agents are moving from simple chat interfaces to autonomous systems that can read documents, call tools, search the web, trigger workflows, and support or trigger business decisions. This creates a new security challenge: we no longer protect only data, but also the agent’s agency.

sessions.title: Web Apps with Superpowers: Breaking the Sandbox with Project Fugu
sessions.speaker: Davide Passafaro
sessions.abstract: For years, the browser was a safe but isolated playground. If you wanted to talk to a Bluetooth device, edit local files, or access a serial port, you had to go native. Not anymore.

sessions.title: Building UIs for AI Products
sessions.speaker: Carlos Guedes
sessions.abstract: AI broke the old rules of frontend development — streaming, uncertain, and increasingly autonomous responses demand new UI patterns. A practical look at what’s changing and how to design for it.

sessions.title: Our SDLC Journey with AI
sessions.speaker: Diego Rodríguez Varela
sessions.abstract: AI is changing how we build software, but its real value comes when it supports the whole SDLC, not only code generation.

sessions.title: What’s New in Git 3
sessions.speaker: Rob Richardson
sessions.abstract: Want to get started with the latest Git features including sha256 and reftable? Worried you’ll need to big-bang convert to Git 3 as soon as the first developer updates? Git 3 is a major rethink of the architecture, but not a major change to the Git user experience.

sessions.title: Before the Agent: Observability for Document Pipelines
sessions.speaker: Duarte Cardoso
sessions.abstract: Agents now ship with observability by default: traces of every call, evaluations of every answer, guardrails on every tool. But most of what an agent knows arrives earlier, through an ingestion pipeline that loads, reads, splits and embeds documents, and that part is a blind spot for many.

sessions.title: Tour of Agent Protocols: MCP, A2A, AG-UI, A2UI
sessions.speaker: Mete Atamel
sessions.abstract: There are many emerging protocols around agents. Model Context Protocol (MCP) standardizes how models and agents access external tools and resources. Agent2Agent Protocol (A2A) defines how agents running on diverse frameworks and platforms communicate.

sessions.title: Infrastructure from Code: The Next Generation of Cloud Management
sessions.speaker: Erwin Staal
sessions.abstract: While Infrastructure as Code (IaC) has become the standard for managing cloud resources using tools like Terraform or Bicep, writing templates can still be a time-consuming and complex task. But what if infrastructure could be automatically inferred from your application code?

sessions.title: Stop Prompting, Start Planning Reliable Agentic AI with Embabel
sessions.speaker: Patrick Baumgartner
sessions.abstract: Large Language Models enable powerful new AI capabilities, but production-grade enterprise agents require more than prompting alone. Prompt chaining often results in non-deterministic behavior, limited traceability, and systems that are difficult to control and test.

sessions.title: Enredos D'Ouro
sessions.speaker: Eduardo Espinheira
sessions.abstract: Nem tudo o que parece… é! Neste workshop dinâmico, os participantes partilham histórias surpreendentes — reais ou inventadas — dentro de um tempo limite. Enquanto recebem feedback, cabe ao público desvendar a verdade. Uma sessão envolvente sobre o poder do enredo, da expressão e da persuasão.

sessions.title: It's All About AI: Reimagining How We Work, Create, and Think
sessions.speaker: Paulo Pereira
sessions.abstract: Generative AI is no longer a distant promise — it's reshaping how we write, design, code, and solve problems, right now.

sessions.title: Cybersecurity meets AI
sessions.speaker: Pedro Vieira
sessions.abstract: A beginner friendly presentation exploring how artificial intelligence is transforming both the attack and defence sides of cybersecurity.

sessions.title: INDUX-R Project Overview
sessions.speaker: Iason Karakostas
sessions.abstract: INDUX-R: Transforming European INDUstrial Ecosystems through eXtended Reality enhanced by human-centric AI and secure, 5G-enabled IoT

sessions.title: The next frontier - agentic collaborative environments.
sessions.speaker: Krzysztof Cieślak
sessions.abstract: AI-agentic developer tools like Claude Code or GitHub Copilot CLI have emerged as a primary way to develop software over the last few months. However, agentic engineering has been a solo story so far - one developer with a dozen agents, moving forward at warp speed.

sessions.title: Human-in-the-Loop, or Human-as-a-Tool?
sessions.speaker: Pedro Ferreira
sessions.abstract: At Sofico, we build and run Miles, the key software behind car finance and leasing for banks and fleets around the world. Real people sit behind that software all day: our front and back office operators, handling contracts, fines, and the endless small tasks that keep the business alive.

sessions.title: Turning Data & AI into Business Value - the DKV Mobility Journey
sessions.speaker: Sonke Iwersen
sessions.abstract: Turning Data & AI into Business Value - the DKV Mobility Journey - TBD

sessions.title: 4 Proven Steps to Scale Your User Group Through Win-Win Tech Partnerships
sessions.speaker: Gabriel Florêncio Alves
sessions.abstract: Since its relaunch, AWS User Group Porto has rapidly grown by embracing a highly collaborative ecosystem strategy instead of operating in a silo.
